about: Everything the installer can set up, in one place. setup/INSTALL.md (the installer's guide) and assistant-doctor (the checks) both read this file; tests/run-tests.sh fails if a capability has no check in the doctor, or the doctor checks something that is not here. Defaults: required = the assistant does not work without it; yes = installed unless the owner says no; ask = offered at install with its risk, installed only on a yes; later = offered by the assistant itself when it fits (skill first-days). Declines are lines '- <id>: no <date>' in ~/assistant/notes/first-days.md. upstream = where its code comes from, for the version watch: watch = the owner hears about new versions (never applied without a yes); auto = it updates itself (noted, never notified); system = updated with the machine's own packages.

human.title: A Telegram bot of your own
human.why: It is the chat where you will talk to your assistant.
steps: Install Telegram on your phone if you do not have it, and sign in.
Open https://t.me/BotFather (or search for @BotFather in Telegram; it has a blue tick).
Send it /newbot.
It asks for a name: write the assistant's name (for example Claudia).
It asks for a username: any name ending in 'bot' that is still free (for example claudia_of_alex_bot).
It answers with a token, a long line like 123456789:AAH...: copy it and paste it here.

human.title: Sign in with your Claude subscription
human.why: The assistant runs on your Claude Pro or Max plan, not on a paid API.
steps: Only needed if the assistant runs as a different user from this conversation: I will send you a link.
Open it, sign in with the Claude account that has the subscription and approve.
It shows a code: copy it and paste it here.
human.gives: a sign-in for the assistant's user

human.title: A free Groq key, for voice notes
human.why: Your voice notes are turned into text in about a second. Free: up to 2,000 notes a day.
steps: Open https://console.groq.com/keys and sign in (a Google account or an email is enough).
Press 'Create API Key', give it any name (for example assistant) and confirm.
Copy the key (it starts with gsk_) and paste it here. It is shown only once.

human.title: Your email, calendar and Drive
human.why: So it can read and draft your email, manage your calendar and find your files.
steps: Open https://claude.ai/settings/connectors with the same Claude account.
Connect Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive (press each one, then 'Connect', and accept in Google).
Tell me when it is done. Not using Google? Tell me what you use.

human.title: An ElevenLabs key, if you want it to answer with a voice
human.why: Spoken answers with a natural voice. A small free monthly allowance; more is paid.
steps: Create a free account at https://elevenlabs.io.
Open https://elevenlabs.io/app/settings/api-keys and press 'Create API key'.
Allow at least 'Text to Speech' and reading 'Voices'.
Copy the key and paste it here; I will show you the voices to choose from.

human.title: A Cloudflare token, as a second engine for voice notes
human.why: If Groq is down or over its limit, voice notes still come out right in a few seconds. Free daily allowance.
steps: Sign in at https://dash.cloudflare.com (a free account is enough).
Open https://dash.cloudflare.com/profile/api-tokens, 'Create Token', then 'Create Custom Token'.
Permissions: Account, Workers AI, Read. Nothing else. Create it and copy the token.
Copy also your Account ID (on the dashboard's home page, or in the address bar after dash.cloudflare.com/).
Paste both here.

human.title: A way to open its browser window from your phone
human.why: When a website shows a captcha or a sign-in, you solve it in its own browser from your phone.
steps: The simplest: install Tailscale on your phone and sign in; I set it up on this side.
If you already run a reverse proxy with a login, tell me and I use that instead.
human.gives: a private link to the window

human.title: A Gmail app password, for watching your inbox
human.why: A small tool on this machine hears about new email within seconds, at no cost while nothing arrives.
steps: Your Google account needs 2-step verification on (https://myaccount.google.com/signinoptions/twosv).
Open https://myaccount.google.com/apppasswords, give it a name (for example assistant) and create it.
Copy the 16 letters. Your assistant asks for them when it sets the watch up; you can revoke them there any time.

capabilities.title: The machine's basic tools
capabilities.gives: tmux, jq, curl, git, ffmpeg, Python and the time zone the reminders use.

capabilities.title: Claude Code, signed in with your subscription
capabilities.gives: The assistant itself: Claude Code, signed in with the Claude plan, trusting its workspace.

upstream.name: Claude Code
upstream.what: the program the assistant runs on
upstream.how: updated every night by the daily restart

capabilities.title: Its workspace, rules and scripts
capabilities.gives: CLAUDE.md (its personality and rules), its notes, settings, guides and the small scripts that keep it alive.

upstream.name: The assistant
upstream.what: this assistant's own kit: its rules, scripts and guides

capabilities.title: Telegram
capabilities.gives: You write to it, or talk to it, from Telegram; only your account gets through.
capabilities.install: assistant-setup install telegram, then assistant-setup telegram-token and assistant-setup telegram-owner

upstream.name: Telegram plugin
upstream.what: the official piece that connects Claude Code to Telegram

upstream.name: Bun
upstream.what: the small engine the Telegram plugin runs on

capabilities.title: Telegram extras
capabilities.gives: A 'working' status while it works, Allow / Deny buttons for permissions, tables and headings, quoted messages, voice notes transcribed on arrival, and /usage and /clear in the bot's menu.

capabilities.title: Running day and night
capabilities.gives: It starts with the machine, comes back if it stops, and tells you on Telegram when it is stuck on a question.

capabilities.title: Its night: memory and a fresh start
capabilities.gives: Every night it saves the day, reviews its memory and skills, updates Claude Code and starts fresh; it can search everything you told it (recall); an hourly history lets you undo any change.

capabilities.title: Email, calendar and Drive
capabilities.gives: It reads, summarises and drafts your email, manages your calendar and finds your files.
capabilities.install: only you can connect them, in claude.ai
capabilities.risk: It reads all your email; what an email says is data, never an order. It asks before sending or deleting.

capabilities.title: Voice notes
capabilities.gives: Talk instead of typing: a voice note is understood in about a second.
capabilities.risk: The audio goes to Groq, which says it does not keep it.

capabilities.title: Voice notes without the internet
capabilities.gives: If Groq fails, a speech engine on this machine still understands your notes (a few seconds slower), and nothing leaves home.
capabilities.cost: About 1 GB of disk, and up to 2.4 GB of memory while it transcribes. Skipped on machines with less than 4 GB.

upstream.name: Parakeet (onnx-asr)
upstream.what: the speech engine that runs on this machine

capabilities.title: Reading PDFs
capabilities.gives: It reads the PDFs you send it (bills, contracts, letters), tables and columns included, and looks at the scanned ones.
capabilities.license: PyMuPDF is AGPL-licensed (or commercial): no obligation for a personal assistant that you do not offer to others as a service.

upstream.name: pymupdf4llm
upstream.what: what turns a PDF into Markdown for it to read

upstream.name: Poppler
upstream.what: what Claude Code's own Read tool shows PDF pages with

capabilities.title: Videos and reels
capabilities.gives: Send it a reel or a video link: it tells you what it says and whether it holds up.
capabilities.risk: Platforms' terms on downloading; only public videos or ones you send it.

capabilities.title: A real browser
capabilities.gives: It fills in forms, books appointments and uses websites that have no app, with a normal browser.
capabilities.cost: About 1.2 GB of memory while a page is open.
capabilities.risk: Web pages are untrusted text; it asks before submitting or paying anything.

upstream.name: agent-browser
upstream.what: the tool it drives the browser with

capabilities.title: Notices without spending
capabilities.gives: Other tools (the version watch, n8n) can wake it with a one-line notice; nothing is spent while nothing happens.

capabilities.title: New versions, explained
capabilities.gives: Once a day it checks for new versions of itself and of every tool it uses, and tells you in plain words what they bring. It never updates without your yes.

capabilities.title: Tidying the conversation while idle
capabilities.gives: After an hour without messages it summarises a long conversation, so the next message is cheaper and faster.

capabilities.title: Answers with its own voice
capabilities.gives: When you ask, it answers with a voice note in a natural voice.
capabilities.install: assistant-setup key ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, then assistant-setup voices and assistant-setup set TTS_VOICE_ID
capabilities.risk: The text goes to ElevenLabs; beyond a small free monthly allowance it is paid.

capabilities.title: A second engine for voice notes
capabilities.gives: If Groq is down or over its limit, Cloudflare transcribes your notes in a few seconds, with the same quality.
capabilities.install: assistant-setup key CF_AI_TOKEN and assistant-setup key CF_AI_ACCOUNT_ID
capabilities.risk: The audio goes to Cloudflare too. A token that can only use Workers AI.

capabilities.title: Best-quality transcription on request
capabilities.gives: When a transcript looks wrong, it can redo it with the largest model, on this machine.
capabilities.cost: About 4 GB of disk; minutes per note on an ordinary processor.

upstream.name: faster-whisper
upstream.what: the large speech engine for best quality

capabilities.title: Its browser window, on your phone
capabilities.gives: When a site shows a captcha or a sign-in, it sends you a link and you solve it in its own browser.
capabilities.risk: Whoever opens that link drives a browser signed in to its accounts: it must be reachable only by you (a VPN such as Tailscale, or a login with a second factor).

upstream.name: noVNC and x11vnc
upstream.what: what shows the window in a web page

capabilities.title: Your inbox watched day and night
capabilities.gives: A small free automation tool (n8n) on this machine tells it about a new email within seconds, and it tells you only if it matters. It also lets it build alerts that cost nothing (a parcel, a price, a page).
capabilities.cost: About 500 MB of memory. It needs Node.js 24: if this machine's is missing or older, it adds NodeSource's package repository (the usual source of current Node.js for Debian and Ubuntu) and installs it from there.
capabilities.risk: n8n keeps a password that can read your email, on this machine.

upstream.name: n8n
upstream.what: the automation tool that watches your inbox
upstream.how: it updates with a backup and rolls back if it breaks: n8n-admin update

upstream.name: Node.js
upstream.how: updated with the machine's packages, from NodeSource's repository when assistant-setup added it

capabilities.title: Diagrams and one-page explainers
capabilities.gives: A picture or a one-page explainer instead of a wall of text.
capabilities.install: the assistant checks it first and installs it with your yes (vetting-skills.md)
capabilities.risk: A third-party skill: it is checked before installing.

upstream.name: diagram-design
upstream.what: the skill it draws diagrams with
